Worked example: Harvest Lane on HubSpot Free, so most logic runs in n8n.

RuleTriggerActionWhere and planOwner

Why n8n: the free plan has very little automation and there is no admin to maintain CRM workflows. If Harvest Lane later pays for a higher plan, the task rules could move into HubSpot. Every n8n rule is documented in the handover pack.
mistakes: Putting lead scoring inside HubSpot Free, where it is not available.
Rules with no owner or no trigger.
Not noting which plan each CRM-side rule needs.
Planning an automation that changes deal stages by itself.
b.pass: A table covering every lead source and follow-up rule, each with a trigger, an action, an owner, where it runs and why, and the plan it needs.
b.redo: Send it back if any rule lacks a trigger, owner or plan note, or an automation moves deal stages.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane, HubSpot Free, private app "n8n Growth Desk" with only contact, company and deal scopes; token in an n8n credential.

CRM · Upsert lead: normalise (lowercase email, +234 phone, domain without www.) → search company by domain, update or create → contact Create or Update by email with lead_source and consent → associate → if buying intent and no open deal, create deal at New enquiry, owner Tolu, associate both → save crm_contact_id and crm_deal_id in Supabase. Called by the Instagram (5.5) and email (5.7) engines.

Score: the lesson's Code node (zone knock-out, base 30, type 20, asked 25, opens 5, size 10, ready at 65) → harvest_score property; ready → SQL and "Call today" task.

Stage change: HubSpot Trigger on dealstage → Switch → Proposal sent creates a follow-up task due in 3 days. It writes only tasks and notes, never the stage.

Ops Agent: AI Agent with read-only search tools plus propose_change (inserts into crm_proposals). Telegram Approve or Reject; a separate executor checks the allow-list in code before calling HubSpot.

TestExpectedResult
Grill Yard enquires on Instagram, then by email (same domain)1 company, 1 contact, 1 deal1 / 1 / 1; second run updated, not created
Move test deal to Proposal sent1 task, workflow runs once1 execution, task due in 3 days
Agent proposes merging two Bodija Suites (same domain); RejectNothing changesProposal status rejected; both companies still there; executor not run
Agent asked to delete contactsRefuses; not on allow-listNo proposal created

Evidence: execution list filtered by workflow, HubSpot record screenshots, and the crm_proposals table.
mistakes: Using 'Create contact' instead of 'Create or Update', so each message makes a new contact.
A stage-change workflow that writes back to the deal and triggers itself.
Giving the Ops Agent HubSpot write tools instead of propose_change only.
Pasting the private app token into a node.
Skipping associations, so deals have no company.
s.pass: Evidence that the same test lead from two channels produced one contact, one company and one deal; a stage change produced exactly one execution; and a rejected Ops Agent proposal left HubSpot unchanged.
s.redo: Send it back if duplicates appear, any workflow runs more than once per change, the agent can write to the CRM directly, or the token is outside a credential.

g.answer:
Worked example: Crestline Uniforms (fictional, from 5.8), one month on HubSpot Free with WhatsApp, email and Instagram feeding CRM · Upsert lead.

Score calibration on last quarter (24 school leads, 6 became customers): weights tuned in code until the call-first list caught all 6 buyers with 2 false alarms; "opened emails" kept at low weight; outside Ogun State = knock-out.

Ops Agent health checkWeek 1Week 2Week 3Week 4
Duplicate companies9410

Open deals with no next step11532
Proposals approved / changed / rejected6 / 2 / 14 / 1 / 12 / 1 / 01 / 0 / 0

Leads typed by hand: 0 of 47 new leads this month.

Deal saved by an alert: Bright Future Academy appeared on the "going cold" list after 7 quiet days at Quote sent. Tayo called; the bursar had lost the quote. Re-sent the same day; deposit of ₦600,000 paid the following week.

Loops and duplicates: no workflow ran more than once per change all month (execution counts checked weekly).

Submit: the calibration table, the four health reports, the deal's timeline, the Monday pipeline reports and the client's note naming the deal.
mistakes: Calibrating the score on guesses instead of last quarter's real outcomes.
Letting the Ops Agent's changes run without the owner's approval.
Claiming a deal was saved with no timeline to show the alert led to it.
Comparing health checks from week 1 and week 4 that measure different things.
g.pass: A month of real use with no leads typed by hand, a score calibrated on last quarter, four health reports showing fewer data problems in week 4 than week 1, and the client naming a deal won or saved by a follow-up or going-cold alert.
g.redo: Send it back if leads were still entered by hand, no deal can be traced to an alert, or the health problems did not fall.
